conditions.text: Reproduce on iOS 18.4 on an iPhone15,2 device — these context values were identical across all events.
Push was not deliverable (push.deliverable = false) in every event, so set that state up as well.
App version is not fixed: 2 events on 1.2.0 and 1 on 1.3.0, so the crash is not tied to a single build in this data.
Push OS permission varied (2 ALLOWED, 1 DENIED) and provider registration varied (2 REGISTERED, 1 MISSING), so neither specific value is required.
Profile consistency also varied (true in 2 events, false in 1), so a consistent profile is not a precondition.
No suspect commit was identified, so there is no code change to point the repro at.

missing_evidence_questions.text: What is the state of the saved-search list (count, ordering, stored index) at the moment loadSavedSearches runs? The packet records only the culprit frame, not the data that makes the index invalid.
Why did no suspect commit surface — is src/modules/search/saved-search.ts simply unchanged in the analyzed range, or was the search inconclusive?
Does the crash reproduce on both 1.2.0 and 1.3.0 in a controlled test, or did the version difference correlate with something else not captured here?
Is push.deliverable = false causally involved or just constant across these 3 events? Does the crash still occur with push deliverable?
Are there additional user actions between navigating to /search and tapping button#saved-searches that the breadcrumbs did not capture?

steps_prose.text: Navigate to /search; this step is present in all 3 events considered.
Tap the button#saved-searches control on that screen, also present in all 3 events.
At that point loadSavedSearches raises RangeError: Invalid saved-search index at src/modules/search/saved-search.ts:18.

summary.text: A RangeError with the message "Invalid saved-search index" is thrown in loadSavedSearches (src/modules/search/saved-search.ts line 18) when a user opens the saved-searches control on the search screen; the packet is based on 3 events.
